source_review.notes: Retrieved and reviewed all ten final destinations: seven PostgreSQL 18 pages, current SQLite query-planning documentation, the MySQL 8.4 ICP documentation, and current DuckDB indexing documentation. Verified the cited scan forms, visibility qualification, composite-key/skip-scan scope, ordering and LIMIT interaction, partial-index implication, planner cost/statistics semantics, index-condition pushdown, and DuckDB zonemap/ART claims. Product-specific behavior is labeled rather than universalized.

evidence: Checked R, S, P(t), E(t), Q(S,R,P,E), candidate-set, selectivity, page-count, leaf-count, distinct-base-page, and cost-coefficient notation.
Checked TRUE-versus-FALSE/UNKNOWN qualification and bag, visibility, projection, residual, lossy recheck, and delivered-order terms remain distinct.
Checked both displayed cost expressions define every variable and are explicitly simplified estimates rather than physical laws.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Logical result, access candidates, visible versions, physical pages, and measured buffer/device events are not conflated.

evidence: Independently enumerated all 96 physical row identifiers and confirmed multiplication by 37 modulo 96 is a bijection.
Recomputed clustered heap pages as 1, 1, 3, 6, 12 and scattered heap pages as 1, 8, 12, 12, 12 for match counts 1, 8, 24, 48, 96.
Recomputed leaf pages as 1, 1, 3, 6, 12 and total modeled index paths, including the corrected 24-row totals of 7 clustered and 16 scattered pages.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The independent record is artifacts/reviews/DBE-052/independent-recomputation.txt. Counts are logical page identities, not measured I/O or latency.

evidence: Reviewed Q(S,R,P,E) as the bag of projected snapshot-visible tuple versions whose three-valued predicate is TRUE.

Reviewed sequential completeness from eligible-location coverage plus conservative pruning, and index completeness/soundness through candidate reachability, locator/version resolution, visibility, and residual recheck.
Reviewed the cost decomposition into startup, search/leaf, distinct base pages, and candidate visibility/predicate work; verified cost comparison is downstream of legality proofs.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The chapter presents a proof structure and conditional cost model, not a universal optimizer theorem.

evidence: Reviewed empty inputs, one/all matches, duplicates, null/UNKNOWN, boundary keys, collations, directions/null placement, ties, and early LIMIT termination.
Reviewed clustered/scattered layouts, narrow/wide rows, covering/noncovering paths, dead or updated versions, partial/expression/composite indexes, lossy summaries, and leading-column omissions.

Reviewed cold/warm cache, skew/parameters, stale statistics, concurrent splits/compaction/reclamation, serializable protection, DML recheck, cancellation, remote retry, missing objects, and corruption/fault behavior.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Unsafe pruning, unknown operator semantics, or expired locator protection must fall back conservatively or fail explicitly.

evidence: Checked every visible qualifying tuple is reached with correct multiplicity and every emitted tuple passes visibility and all residual/lossy conditions.
Checked navigation depends on compatible type, operator class, collation, expression, and index predicate semantics.
Checked delivered order, early stop, locking/isolation, resource cleanup, and plan-evidence environment binding are separate obligations.
invariant_checking.notes: Candidate discovery is never described as final SQL qualification.

evidence: Reviewed the sequential proof as physical coverage, conservative-pruning soundness, version visibility, predicate truth, and projection.
Reviewed the index proof as candidate completeness, maintained locator resolution, visibility, residual soundness, and fallback where completeness cannot be established.
Reviewed index-only value/visibility obligations and ordered-delivery proof including comparator, direction, null, collation, batching, and parallel merge boundaries.
proof_review.notes: Implementation-specific maintenance protocols remain obligations for the target engine and are not proven by the chapter.

evidence: The executable is labeled a finite logical page-touch model and explicitly excludes cache, concurrency, MVCC, compression, prefetch, CPU, and real device latency.
PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, and DuckDB mechanisms are scoped to their cited current documentation rather than promoted to universal database behavior.
Formal scan obligations, estimated cost, observed runtime evidence, plan shape, and production fitness are separated throughout.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No worked example or page count is presented as a hardware benchmark or universal crossover.

evidence: Repository verification passed the standard-library Python snippet with exact six-line stdout, empty stderr, zero exit status, and recorded Python 3.14.4 toolchain.
Independent recomputation reproduced the permutation, heap/leaf page counts, and three comparative crossover claims.
All ten references were retained under artifacts/references/DBE-052 and all repository-local links resolved.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live DBMS scan, EXPLAIN ANALYZE, MVCC/concurrency schedule, cold/warm storage run, benchmark, write-amplification measurement, or production workload was executed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed the progression from logical visible-bag contract through sequential mechanics, index navigation/recheck, composite sargability, index-only visibility, ordering, page-locality cost, estimation, storage/concurrency lifecycle, and verification. Model, guarantee, mechanism, implementation, policy, and evidence are distinguished.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed plan diagnosis using estimates/actuals, loops/searches, candidate/filter/recheck counts, base fetches, cache/device evidence, parameters/statistics, concurrency and isolation. Remedies prioritize semantics, statistics, schema/index/workload design, representative gates, write/recovery cost, and reversible scoped controls.

pedagogical_review.notes: The chapter starts from the scan result contract, derives the access-path proof, uses a corrected executable locality model, supplies twelve misconceptions and ten distinct worked examples, and progresses through five exercises from terminology to unfamiliar multi-tier design with complete model answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary-source, mathematical, executable-snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, PostgreSQL/MySQL/SQLite/DuckDB or storage-engine maintainer, standards, security, performance, reliability, operations, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and finite model prove neither universal scan/index equivalence, correctness of any named engine, safe behavior for every type/collation/MVCC/index method/concurrency schedule, estimator or cost-model accuracy, actual cache/device/parallel/remote performance, workload-independent index value, certification, nor deployment fitness.
